Andy Robertson has emphasized that strengthening Liverpool's defensive performance will be crucial if Arne Slot is to mount a serious title challenge during his debut season as manager. The team has managed to keep a clean sheet in both of their opening games, but they are now preparing for a much tougher test as they travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United on Sunday, where their defensive line will undoubtedly be pushed harder than it has been so far. Neither Ipswich nor Brentford were able to score against Liverpool, giving Slot an ideal beginning to his tenure at the club.

handle the defensive statistics from the previous season, and they paint a telling picture. Liverpool allowed 41 goals throughout their 38 league games last season, ultimately finishing in third place. That figure was seven goals more than champions Manchester City conceded, and a significant 12 more than Arsenal, who finished as runners-up. Despite this, Robertson acknowledged that the encouraging early results offer reason for optimism. He reflected on the two clean sheets they have secured so far, describing them as the best possible start they could have hoped for. He expressed hope that this defensive solidity would continue against Manchester United and throughout the rest of the season as well. Robertson pointed out that even when Liverpool were still in contention for the title last season, they were consistently giving away more opportunities than their rivals Arsenal and Manchester City. He noted that allowing so many chances inevitably leads to being punished at some point, and that was precisely what happened to Liverpool as their title challenge ultimately faded. His comments suggest a recognition within the squad that defensive improvement is not just desirable but absolutely necessary if they are to compete with the best teams over the course of a full season.

Robertson's reflections highlight a clear-eyed understanding of what went wrong last term and what needs to change for Liverpool to go one better this time around. The fact that Slot has already managed to instill greater defensive discipline in just two matches is an encouraging sign, though the true test of their progress will come in more challenging fixtures like the one at Manchester United. If Liverpool can address the defensive vulnerabilities that undermined their campaign last season while maintaining their attacking threat, they will be in a much stronger position to push for the title. Robertson's words suggest the squad is fully aware of what is required and is determined to put things right under their new manager this season.

P.S. Robertson's comments reflect both honest self-assessment and genuine optimism about Liverpool's potential under Arne Slot's management this season.
